title: Oracle Layoffs Hit Abilene, the 'Flagship' Site of Its OpenAI Stargate Deal
excerpt: The Times of India reports the layoffs have reached the flagship Stargate data center in Abilene, Texas — the site Oracle keeps citing as proof its OpenAI deal is on track — as the company cuts up to 30,000 jobs to fund a $50 billion AI buildout.
body:
• Oracle's layoffs have reached its Abilene, Texas data center campus — the flagship Stargate site the company keeps citing as proof its OpenAI partnership is on track, according to The Times of India.
  • An Oracle Cloud Infrastructure employee wrote on Reddit's r/employeesOfOracle that he learned he had been fired only when his badge failed at the site gate; internal Slack membership fell by about 3,200 people as US cuts hit OCI, Fusion, NetSuite and Oracle Health.
  • Reported severance terms amount to four weeks' pay plus a week per year served, capped at 26 weeks, while a fresh India wave is reported at roughly 3,000 jobs — figures Oracle has not confirmed.
  • The cuts are part of a planned reduction of up to 30,000 jobs in 2026 to fund a $50 billion AI buildout — even as free cash flow turned negative $24.7 billion and total debt hit about $134.6 billion.

The cuts reach Abilene

Oracle's rolling layoffs have now reached Abilene, Texas — the flagship data center campus Oracle keeps pointing to as proof its OpenAI deal is fine, according to The Times of India. The cuts hit Oracle Cloud Infrastructure and other units at the very site where the Stargate partnership is supposed to be taking physical shape.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=DYvGvKLaltg

For the workers affected, the way the news arrived was almost as brutal as the news itself. One OCI employee wrote on Reddit's r/employeesOfOracle that he learned he had been fired when his badge failed at the gate. Company-wide, internal Slack membership dropped by about 3,200 people as US reductions hit OCI, Fusion, NetSuite and Oracle Health.

"He learned he had been fired only when his badge failed at the gate."

— OCI employee, in a post on r/employeesOfOracle reported by The Times of India

Severance terms — and a new India wave

Reported severance terms include four weeks of pay plus one week for every year served, capped at 26 weeks, per Firstpost and Inshorts. The same reporting says a fresh round of job cuts in India has affected around 3,000 employees. Oracle has not confirmed any of the figures.

The layoffs are part of a program announced earlier this year to cut up to 30,000 jobs in 2026 to free cash for the AI buildout. Trailing free cash flow has swung to negative $24.7 billion, and Oracle has borrowed roughly $43 billion specifically for AI data centers. After a $30 billion debt-and-equity raise in February 2026, total debt stands near $134.6 billion and FY26 capex guidance is $50 billion — about 3.5 times the FY24 level. An earlier wave had already hit teams in India, Canada and the US.

What Stargate is — and why Abilene matters

Stargate is the $500 billion AI infrastructure initiative announced at the White House in January 2025, with OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank as founding partners. The Abilene campus — developed and operated by Crusoe — is its flagship: the first Stargate site to go live, with 1.2 gigawatts of Nvidia Blackwell capacity.

But the flagship has been wobbling. Plans to expand Abilene to 2 gigawatts were scrapped in March 2026, Bloomberg reported, after financing talks collapsed and a winter cooling outage strained the OpenAI–Crusoe relationship. Nvidia has since paid Crusoe a $150 million deposit and is lining up Meta as a new tenant. Oracle insists the broader 4.5 GW agreement with OpenAI remains on track.

"The broader 4.5 GW agreement with OpenAI remains on track."

— Oracle's position, per reporting

Why layoffs at the flagship send a signal

Companies in expansion mode do not usually shrink headcount at the site they are selling as evidence of momentum. Cutting staff at Abilene while telling investors the OpenAI deal is fine creates a tension that is hard to spin away — the kind of detail that has Stargate skeptics asking whether the $500 billion ambition is on schedule.

The financials explain the lever. A $50 billion capex program against negative $24.7 billion in trailing free cash flow means the buildout is being financed with borrowed money — and layoffs are the other side of that ledger.

The diaspora angle

Oracle employs thousands of Indian engineers in the US and India, and the reported India wave alone runs to roughly 3,000 jobs — a direct hit on the diaspora tech workforce. For those on employer-sponsored visas, a layoff also sharpens immigration stakes: under long-standing USCIS policy, laid-off visa holders generally have a 60-day grace period to find a new sponsor or change status.

What's next

Oracle has not said whether the Abilene reductions are complete, and the 30,000-job program has months to run. Next tests: earnings updates, whether the 4.5 GW OpenAI agreement stays intact, whether Meta takes space at Abilene — and whether the flagship Oracle keeps citing looks like momentum, or like a warning.
